html:
SMTO-EML-0006 — SMTO couldn't connect to your mail server

GUID: 3f937e12-1331-5b2b-bbbd-a916ef26f08b
Slug: email-dns-failed
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't reach your mail server, or the server hung up during the opening exchange. This happened before your message was handed over, so no email went out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu, select your email sender profile, and check the server name and port are exactly what your email provider gives. A typo in the server name or a wrong port means SMTO can't find or reach the server.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on the Gateway you use. Make sure that computer is switched on and connected to the internet or your company network. The Gateway, not your browser, is what connects to the mail server.
  3. Ask your IT team whether a firewall blocks outgoing mail ports such as 587 or 465 from that computer. Many networks block mail ports, which makes connections fail or time out.
  4. Ask SMTO in a conversation to test the email connection for that sender profile. When it reports the server is ready, ask SMTO to send your email again. The test confirms SMTO can reach the server without sending anything.

What success looks like

  • The connection test reports the mail server is ready, and your email is accepted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your network or mail server, saying which Gateway you used, since the problem may affect only that computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's SMTP client failed during connection setup (DNS resolution, connection refused or timed out, non-220 greeting, non-250 EHLO, or another connection or protocol error) before any message data was transmitted.

What this means

  • SMTP greeting/EHLO is rejected or a connection/protocol/encoding exception occurs outside an unresolved message-transmission phase. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • SMTP greeting/EHLO is rejected or a connection/protocol/encoding exception occurs outside an unresolved message-transmission phase.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect last_confirmed_stage and numeric reply/exception class before attributing the problem to DNS or routing.

How to fix it

  • Check error_kind (email_dns_failed, email_connection_refused, email_connection_timeout, email_greeting_invalid, email_ehlo_failed or email_connection_failed), last_confirmed_stage and any smtp_response_code. From the Gateway host verify DNS for the profile's server, reachability of server:port (for example nc -vz host 587), outbound firewall rules, and the profile's timeout_seconds.
  • Resolve the recorded SMTP connection or protocol failure and inspect the original delivery evidence before deciding whether to send again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The specific protocol or connection issue is resolved and receipt evidence permits any new send.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
